answer: Each identity stakes one timber log and locks 60 credits. A raven auditor cuts an ember-heated core sample, counts its rings, and posts the count publicly; only logs with at least 40 rings qualify, so no identity can be grown overnight. Seasoned logs are finite: the k-th fake needs a fresh old log at 50+3(k-1) credits, so the 1000th costs 3047, and 1000 fakes pay 1548500 plus 60000 locked. Renting one log fails, because a second sample reuses the same ledger entry and both bonds burn. An honest agent buys one 50-credit log, locks 60 once, and recovers it after a clean epoch.
